solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Ambience? A most peculiar piano in this place (10)

indicatorNotes.peculiar: a peculiar MOST has its letters out of their usual order

blocks.note: p = piano, the musical marking for soft

annotation.surface: Someone remarks that a room with a very odd piano in it has a strange ambience.
annotation.walkthrough: "A most peculiar" reads as one phrase of mild astonishment, but the A stands alone and only MOST is jumbled.
annotation.definitionFit: The atmosphere of a place is its ambience, its prevailing mood.

entries.clue: Recording almost entirely useless, from America (5)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost all of a word: drop its last letter

blocks.note: bum is American slang for worthless, as in a bum deal

annotation.surface: A critic dismisses an American recording as almost entirely useless.
annotation.walkthrough: "From America" flags that BUM is being used in its US adjective sense, not the British one.
annotation.definitionFit: An album is a recording issued as a collection of tracks.

entries.clue: Answer not hard to see in golf? Male coming over, being patronising? (12)

annotation.definitionNote: the verb phrase 'being patronising' stands for the -ing form describing what a man does

indicatorNotes.coming over: in a down clue, a piece coming over the rest sits on top of it

blocks.note: ans. is the standard abbreviation for answer
G is golf in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A man at the golf course condescendingly explains something that was obvious anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue's first words look like the start, but M for "Male" goes on top of everything else because this is a down answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Mansplaining is a man explaining something in a patronising way, usually to a woman who already knows it.

entries.clue: Second family hide (4)

blocks.note: s = second, the unit of time

annotation.surface: A second family has to go into hiding.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hide" looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal's skin.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the leather-trade sense: a tanner works an animal's pelt whether you call it the hide or the skin.

entries.clue: Meal for Macbeth? Witches bringing in good one (6)

indicatorNotes.bringing in: the outer word brings the inner letters inside itself

blocks.note: hags = witches, as in Macbeth's three

annotation.surface: Macbeth's witches arrive with a good dish for his supper.
annotation.walkthrough: Macbeth is a Scottish king, so his meal is the Scottish dish haggis, a sheep's offal pudding; the question mark marks the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Haggis is the national dish of Scotland, fitting fare for a Scottish king.

entries.clue: Rare slip after arranging retaliation (8)

indicatorNotes.after arranging: the letters are what you have after arranging them anew

annotation.surface: An unusual mistake draws a vengeful response once someone has sorted things out.
annotation.walkthrough: "After arranging" reads as a time phrase in the surface, but it tells you to rearrange RARE SLIP.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name a hitting back at an enemy for harm done, as when a raid provokes reprisals.

entries.clue: Film comedian repaired broken statue (6,6)

indicatorNotes.repaired: a repaired thing has had its parts put back in a new order

annotation.surface: A film comedian mends a statue that has been smashed.
annotation.walkthrough: "Broken" is not the indicator here but part of the fodder; "repaired" does the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was a star comedian of silent films.

entries.clue: Regret a lot of painful argument (6)

indicatorNotes.a lot of: a lot of a word, but not all: its last letter goes

annotation.surface: Someone regrets a long and painful quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: ROW here rhymes with cow: a quarrel, not a line.
annotation.definitionFit: Both nouns name the sadness felt over something done or lost: to express sorrow for an error is to express regret.

entries.clue: Suggestion from republican finance industry? (7)

blocks.note: split in two, it is the proposal an anti-monarchist would make: get rid of the monarch
the business of lending, deposits and loans, taken as a whole sector

annotation.surface: A republican proposes something about the banking sector.
annotation.walkthrough: A republican here means someone opposed to monarchy, whose suggestion would be to BAN (the) KING.
annotation.definitionFit: Banking is the business of banks, the core of the finance industry.

entries.clue: Start to patronise London airport skipping new destination for extended flight? (5)

indicatorNotes.Start to: the start of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.skipping: skipping a letter leaves it out

annotation.surface: A traveller disdains Luton airport as a starting point for a long flight.
annotation.walkthrough: Luton is one of London's airports; the flight that is really meant is a space probe's, such as NASA's nine-year trip to Pluto.
annotation.definitionFit: Pluto is so far off that reaching it took a spacecraft years of flight.

entries.clue: Be glum as motorcycle loses rear end (4)

indicatorNotes.loses rear end: the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: this D is the last letter, the one lost

annotation.surface: A rider feels miserable because their motorbike's back end has fallen off.
annotation.walkthrough: The rider's gloom in the surface is the definition itself, which is why the clue reads so smoothly.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in verb form: to mope about is to be glum and listless, sulking without purpose.

entries.clue: Spray enveloping popular member of cabinet (8)

indicatorNotes.enveloping: the outer word wraps round the inner one

blocks.note: a mister is a device that sprays fine droplets

annotation.surface: A popular politician is caught in a spray, perhaps of protest.
annotation.walkthrough: "Spray" is the noun for the spraying gadget, not the droplets.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the cabinet is the group of senior government heads of department, each holding that title.

entries.clue: Very precise individual line in adhesive label (8)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece sits in the other

blocks.note: a sticker is an adhesive label

annotation.surface: A pedant insists that a label carry a single exact line.
annotation.walkthrough: "Individual" is a noun here, part of the definition, not an adjective describing the line.
annotation.definitionFit: A stickler is someone who insists on exactness.

entries.clue: Cordiality and warmth welcoming traveller at last (5)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: the outer word welcomes a letter inside it
indicatorNotes.at last: the last letter of the word before

annotation.surface: A host greets a late-arriving traveller with friendliness and warmth.
annotation.walkthrough: "Warmth" looks like a second definition beside "Cordiality", but it is the wordplay's HEAT.
annotation.definitionFit: Heart can mean warmth of feeling, as in speaking with heart.

entries.clue: Religious book extreme elements of holy men are loving at the outset (6)

indicatorNotes.extreme elements of: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.at the outset: the outset of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: first and last letters of holy
first and last letters of men

annotation.surface: The book says holy men are loving from the very start.
annotation.walkthrough: Two different selectors share the clue: outer letters for the first two words, first letters for the last two.
annotation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns used in church.

entries.clue: Missile transporter missing opening (5)

indicatorNotes.missing opening: the word lacks its first letter

blocks.note: a barrow is a small cart for carrying loads
this B is the opening letter, the one missing

annotation.surface: A missile launcher vehicle is missing its hatch.
annotation.walkthrough: "Missile transporter" reads as one military vehicle, but it splits into definition and wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: any projectile is a missile, and the one loosed from a bow is the oldest kind.

entries.clue: Annoys park wardens, blowing top (6)

indicatorNotes.blowing top: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and it is blown away

blocks.note: rangers look after parks and forests
this R sits at the top of the down entry and is blown off

annotation.surface: Someone annoys the park rangers until they lose their temper.
annotation.walkthrough: "Blowing top" suggests losing one's temper, but it takes the top letter off.
annotation.definitionFit: To anger someone is to annoy them.

entries.clue: Intimidating blokes acting out of turn to begin with (8)

indicatorNotes.out of: one letter goes out of the word
indicatorNotes.to begin with: only the first letter of turn is meant

blocks.clueFragment: acting out of turn to begin with
blocks.note: ACTING without T, the first letter of turn

annotation.surface: Some men behaving badly and out of turn seem threatening.
annotation.walkthrough: "Acting out of turn" is an idiom for misbehaving, but here it removes a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both adjectives: a menacing look and an intimidating look both carry a threat.

entries.clue: Unproductive, with no soil, with no carbon (4)

indicatorNotes.with no: the word appears with no C in it

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon, the letter removed

annotation.surface: Land is barren because it has no soil and no carbon in it.
annotation.walkthrough: "With no soil" feels like part of a barren field; it is CLEAN, unsoiled.
annotation.definitionFit: A lean year or season is one that produces little.

entries.clue: Appropriate place, hot, in French resort (5)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece sits in the other

blocks.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
h = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A tourist finds a suitably hot spot in Nice.
annotation.walkthrough: The spelling Nice is the capitalised French city, not the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A niche is a place or role that suits someone.

entries.clue: Asian resort erected one experimental location (4)

indicatorNotes.erected: in a down clue, erected means set upright, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a lab is where experiments are done

annotation.surface: An Asian holiday spot puts up a single research facility.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversed LAB comes first even though "one" is written before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island popular with holidaymakers.

entries.clue: Cancel regular publication after second article rejected (5)

indicatorNotes.rejected: the article is rejected, thrown out of the word

blocks.note: a book or magazine issued once a year
a is the indefinite article; the second A in the word is the one thrown out

annotation.surface: An editor cancels a yearly magazine after its second article is turned down.
annotation.walkthrough: "Second article" means the second A in ANNUAL, not a second piece of writing.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: a court that annuls a marriage cancels it, declaring it void.

entries.clue: Flexible element in the last ice-cap (7)

indicatorNotes.element in: the answer is an element, a part, found in the words that follow

annotation.surface: Something pliable is found in the last polar ice-cap.
annotation.walkthrough: "Element" suggests chemistry, but here it just means a part of the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both adjectives, used of materials and figuratively of rules or schedules that bend.

entries.clue: Foresight regarding Southern Channel Islands during change (10)

indicatorNotes.during: these letters come during the other word, inside it

annotation.surface: A forecaster predicts how currency in the southern Channel Islands will change.
annotation.walkthrough: PENCE are British coins, the everyday small change in one's pocket.
annotation.definitionFit: Prescience is knowing about things before they happen.
